comparison: Perfect agreement on C1, C10, C11. Both evaluations find the heparin/HS binding data from SPR and heparin-Sepharose chromatography well-supported with appropriate methods. All reviewers affirm these findings as compelling and rigorous.

Perfect agreement on C3, C12-C15. Both evaluations find the mutagenesis data identifying the three basic residues in the N-terminus well-supported. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm the binding site identification with no concerns raised.

Strong agreement on C2, C17-C24 regarding oligomerization. Both find SEC-MALS and SAXS data well-supported. Peer review R3 also includes C25, C107, C119, C134 which OpenEval addresses separately, but core oligomerization findings are consistently affirmed as 'nicely showed' and 'well supported.'

Perfect agreement on C40-C44. Both evaluations find the flow cytometry data demonstrating HS-dependent cell surface binding well-supported with appropriate controls (heparin lyase III, R115A mutant). Described as 'solid evidence' by both.

Strong agreement on C26-C30, C109, C137 regarding crystal structure and strand swapping. Both find the structural determination well-supported with good refinement statistics. Peer review includes C138-C140 (speculation about hTRAIL) which OpenEval addresses separately as uncertain (R13, R19).

Strong agreement on C8, C80-C83 regarding ternary complex formation. Both evaluations find the heparin-Sepharose chromatography data demonstrating TRAIL-HS-DR5 complex well-supported. Peer review also includes C108, C132 related to broader mechanistic implications.

Strong agreement on C9, C84-C88, C126, C128-C129, C131 regarding DR5 internalization. Both find the flow cytometry internalization data well-supported and note the novel finding that DR5 internalization is HS-dependent despite DR5 not binding HS directly. Peer review suggests mechanistic interpretation is incomplete and recommends DR4 data.

Agreement on C4, C45-C47, C50 regarding apoptosis in MDA-MB-453 cells. Both find the Annexin V and TUNEL data well-supported. OpenEval R6 also covers C48-C51 (heparin blocking) which peer review addresses in R7. Core apoptosis findings described as 'compelling' and 'solid evidence.'

Agreement on C58-C60 regarding R115A mutant effects. Both evaluations find this functional validation of the HS-binding site well-supported. OpenEval R7 also covers C52-C56 (dose-response in other cells) which peer review addresses in R6 and R12. Mutant data directly links binding to function.

Partial overlap on C52-C54 regarding apoptosis in RPMI-8226 and U266 cells. OpenEval finds dose-response data well-supported showing partial HS dependence. Peer review R6 broadly affirms apoptosis data across cell lines as 'compelling' evidence.

Agreement on C48-C49, C51 regarding heparin blocking of apoptosis. Both evaluations find the competitive inhibition data well-supported. Peer reviewer 2 explicitly states this point is 'supported well' and raises important clinical implications.

Agreement on C5, C106 regarding heparin blocking effects. Both find the experimental data well-supported. OpenEval R14 also covers C147-C151 (clinical implications) which peer review addresses in R13, noting importance but requiring further validation for clinical extrapolations.

Agreement on C61-C64 regarding proportional reduction in apoptosis across cell lines. Both find the data well-supported showing HS plays a general role. Peer review R8 extensively covers correlation claims (C6-C7, C65-C79, C145-C146) which OpenEval addresses in R9.

Significant disagreement on C6-C7, C65-C79, C145-C146 regarding HS expression correlation with TRAIL sensitivity. OpenEval finds correlation supported but notes it's correlative with only three cell lines. Peer reviewers express stronger concerns: correlation is 'still correlative and will need further investigation' and HS 'does not play a sole determining role.' Both note causation not established.

Agreement on C122-C125 regarding differential HS dependence based on receptor expression. Both evaluations acknowledge this finding, with peer reviewer 2 explicitly discussing the differential effects in MDA-MB-453 vs. high-receptor cells. OpenEval finds the receptor-density model reasonable; peer review suggests mechanistics 'could have been more clearly defined.'

Partial agreement on C143-C144, C146 regarding HS as resistance mechanism. OpenEval finds this supported but notes correlation based on only three cell lines. Peer review is more uncertain, noting the relationship is 'still correlative' and HS is not a 'sole determining role.' Both agree further validation needed.

Partial overlap on C147, C150-C151 regarding clinical implications of heparin interference. OpenEval finds experimental data supported but clinical extrapolations speculative. Peer review notes the point is 'important' and 'supported well' but also expresses concerns about whether HS is determinative. Both note in vivo validation needed.

Agreement on C31-C33, C138-C139 regarding speculation about hTRAIL strand swapping. OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting the conclusion is speculative without direct experimental evidence. Peer review R4 includes these claims but describes overall structural work as 'well supported,' though functional significance acknowledged as speculative.

Agreement on C140, C153-C154 regarding future research directions. OpenEval rates as uncertain, noting these are hypotheses for Discussion rather than supported conclusions. Peer review R4 includes C140 within structural findings but does not specifically evaluate the speculative nature of functional consequences.

Partial overlap on C34-C39, C134-C136 (SAXS data). OpenEval finds SAXS data well-supported and consistent with SEC-MALS. Peer review R3 affirms oligomerization findings including SAXS as 'nicely showed' and 'well supported.' Both evaluations agree on the quality of biophysical characterization.

Minimal overlap on C103-C105, C107-C108, C110-C112, C118, C152 (main conclusions). OpenEval finds main conclusions well-supported by comprehensive data. Peer review R6 affirms apoptosis findings as 'compelling' but addresses specific experimental claims rather than synthesized conclusions.

Minimal overlap on C108 (ternary complex in conclusions). OpenEval finds overall conclusions well-supported. Peer review R9 specifically affirms ternary complex formation with 'solid evidence.' Both agree on this mechanistic finding.

Minimal overlap on C20 (SEC-MALS MW determination). OpenEval specifically validates this measurement as confirming expected oligomeric state. Peer review R3 includes this within broader oligomerization findings described as 'well supported.'

Minimal overlap on C25 (hTRAIL precipitation). OpenEval rates as uncertain regarding mechanism. Peer review R3 includes this observation within oligomerization findings but does not specifically evaluate the precipitation mechanism.
